newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Macedonian power line downs UN chopper, 4 dead.
newsitem.headline: Macedonian power line downs UN chopper, 4 dead.

text.p: Three Finnish U.N. peacekeepers, one of them a woman, and their Canadian civilian pilot died when their helicopter struck a power line in Macedonia on Saturday, Macedonian television reported.

It said the helicopter's rotor blade struck the cable, there was an explosion and the aircraft plunged into Mavrovo lake about 20 km (12 miles) south of the border between Macedonia, the Serbian-ruled province of Kosovo and Albania.

Earlier, Finland's STT news agency said all three passengers -- a major, a captain and a U.N. battalion's female dentist -- as well as the pilot died when the helicopter crashed. Two bodies were found.
The Finns were among 360 engaged in a U.N. operation with the pan-Nordic battalion.
The Finnish defence ministry named the dead as Major Risto Vuori, Captain Tapani Kulmala and dentist Kaisa Arvola, STT said.
Female volunteers have been accepted into Finnish military service since 1995. U.N. peacekeeping duty is voluntary.
STT said the cause of the crash was unclear, but it quoted the Defence Ministry as saying it was clearly an accident, possibly caused by a collision with an overhead power line.
Macedonian television said an investigation was underway and rescue workers were still trying to locate the remains of the two other victims.
